name: Aggressive Primary Cutaneous T-Cell Lymphoma
aliases: Primary Cutaneous Peripheral T-Cell Lymphoma, Aggressive Type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO-EORTC Classification for Primary Cutaneous Lymphomas

criteria.description: Presence of dense dermal infiltrate of atypical T-cells with epidermotropism and cytologic atypia
T-cell phenotype with CD3+, CD4+/CD8- or CD8+ aberrant expression and loss of pan-T-cell markers
Rapidly progressive cutaneous plaques, tumors, or ulcerations without extracutaneous involvement at diagnosis
Clonal T-cell receptor gene rearrangement detected by PCR
Exclusion of systemic T-cell lymphoma with secondary skin involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathologic confirmation of atypical T-cell infiltrate with compatible immunophenotype and clinical presentation, plus exclusion of systemic lymphoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, histological, immunophenotypic, and molecular findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Rapidly enlarging cutaneous tumors with ulceration
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic aggressive skin lesions often ulcerate

searchTerms: skin infiltration by unusual immune cells
clusters of red plaques and nodules

common.symptomName: Constitutional symptoms including low-grade fever and weight loss

occasional.symptomName: Peripheral neuropathy due to nerve infiltration

searchTerms: frequent infections due to low immunity

laboratory: Clonal T-cell receptor gene rearrangement by PCR
imaging: PET-CT showing localized skin lesions without systemic involvement at diagnosis
Ultrasound or CT of regional lymph nodes
other: Histopathology demonstrating epidermotropism and atypical lymphoid infiltrate
Immunophenotyping showing aberrant T-cell marker expression

distinguishingFeatures: Patch and plaque stages preceding tumors
Systemic symptoms and organ involvement at presentation

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin tumors with ulceration
Failure to respond to standard cutaneous lymphoma therapies
Development of systemic symptoms such as fever, weight loss, and night sweats
references: Willemze R, Jaffe ES, Burg G, et al. WHO-EORTC classification for cutaneous lymphomas. Blood. 2005;105(10):3768-3785.

Bekkenk MW, Geelen FA, van Voorst Vader PC, et al. Primary and secondary cutaneous CD30(+) lymphoproliferative disorders: a report from the Dutch Cutaneous Lymphoma Group on the long-term follow-up data of 219 patients and guidelines for diagnosis and treatment. Blood. 2000;95(12):3653-3661.
Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al., editors. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
